blocks.x: The working definition of Quantum Optimization for Enterprise Problems at Dataq Software: scope we sign, the cadence you can plan around, platform evidence generated in-flight, and outcomes measured against your baseline.

Optimization is where quantum methods earn money today — mostly via hybrid and quantum-inspired solvers on real hardware and HPC. We formulate your problem honestly: constraint modeling of vehicle routing, crew and maintenance scheduling, bin packing, portfolio construction or process formulations; then a solver tournament runs your problem across classical MIP/CP, quantum-inspired (simulated annealing, tensor-network methods, digital annealers) and hybrid QAOA-class approaches on identical benchmarks.

Where a solver wins, we industrialize it: solver-as-a-service integration into planning systems, warm-start pipelines from historical solutions, and re-solve SLAs aligned to operational cadence. Where none beats the baseline, you get the baseline improved and the negative result documented — a rare and valuable deliverable in this field.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
